rules: A divider is a line of thickness in lineColor that separates two groups of content (sections of a panel, groups of fields, the items of a vertical list). Spacing around it comes from the layout that holds it: the divider adds no margin of its own. Space alone, or a container edge, is preferred where it is enough; a divider is not drawn between every block.

horizontal spans the inline size it is given. vertical separates items laid out in a row (a toolbar of filters, metadata on one line): it spans the block size of the row, or the line box of the surrounding text when the row gives it none, and keeps its thickness when space runs out.

label, when set on a horizontal divider, shows short plain text centered on the line (Or, Today) in typography and labelColor, on one line, with labelGap between the text and the line on both sides; the line is drawn on both sides of the text. A vertical divider ignores label.

By default the divider is exposed as a separator with its orientation (and its label as its accessible name when set). When decorative is true it is hidden from assistive technology, for a line that only repeats the structure the content already gives (between items of a list that is announced as a list).
The divider is never focusable, emits no events and has no state; it is not a resize handle.
In forced-colors mode the line and the label use the system text color, so that the line stays visible.
